Legal.draftNotice: Draft for the owner’s review. These texts describe the planned public deployment and apply only once it opens. This build is not connected to the Hyphae Consensus API.

terms.lead: These terms apply to the public Hyphae Consensus portal. They are short: please read them before you start a run.

what.heading: What this portal is
what.body: Hyphae Consensus is an independent research prototype built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026. It shows how three AI roles, a runtime that checks evidence, a fixed policy and a human decision fit together. It is not a commercial product or a professional service, and it is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Meta.

items.age: You must be 18 or older. Live runs ask you to confirm your age before they start.
items.territories: Access to the whole portal is blocked, at country level, from the 21 territories listed as restricted in Meta’s <geo>Geographic Use Policy</geo>. Hong Kong and Macau are blocked as part of China. All of Ukraine is blocked, because the listed Crimea, Donetsk and Luhansk regions cannot be told apart from the rest of the country at country level. South Korea is blocked for live mode only, because Meta’s Muse Wonder model is not available there.

live.heading: Live mode runs presets only
live.body: Live Meta runs start only from curated preset tasks: you cannot send your own text to the model. Live mode has a daily budget. When it is used up, or when live mode is busy, the portal offers a recorded run instead.

use.heading: Acceptable use
use.body: Live runs use Meta’s Model API, so your use of the portal must follow Meta’s <aup>Acceptable Use Policy</aup>. In particular:

items.bypass: Do not try to get around the presets, the limits, the territory block or the bot check.
items.harm: Do not use the portal to harm, deceive or harass anyone.
items.human: Do not present the portal’s outputs as written by a person.

outputs.heading: AI-generated outputs
outputs.body: In live runs, proposals, critiques and evaluations are generated by Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 model. They may be wrong, incomplete or inconsistent, and they are labeled as AI-generated. Guided runs are scripted, and recorded runs replay earlier model outputs. Check anything that matters independently.

execution.heading: Nothing is executed
execution.body: The portal never executes a recommendation: it runs no code from a proposal, changes no repository and takes no action beyond its own records and the calls it makes to Meta’s Model API and to Cloudflare Turnstile. Approving a recommendation only records a decision.

authority.heading: Public decisions carry no authority
authority.body: Decisions recorded by visitors are demonstrations. They are labeled as public demo decisions and carry no authority over any project, system or person.

asis.heading: Provided as is
asis.body: The portal is a research prototype provided as is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, including fitness for a particular purpose. To the extent the law allows, the owner is not liable for damage arising from its use or from acting on its outputs. Nothing in these terms limits rights that consumer law grants you and that cannot be waived.

availability.heading: Availability
availability.body: The portal runs during and shortly after the hackathon. It may be limited, paused or closed at any time, for example when its budget is reached, and run files are deleted after 7 days (the <privacy>Privacy notice</privacy> says what remains).

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.body: The <privacy>Privacy notice</privacy> explains what the portal processes and for how long.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Questions about these terms go to the owner, Mario Gutiérrez: {contact}.

privacy.lead: This notice describes what the planned public deployment of the portal processes. This build is not connected to the API: it stores no runs and no settings on a server (your settings stay in your browser), while the host and Cloudflare keep request logs as described below.

items.none: No analytics or tracking scripts in the pages, no advertising, and no sale of data.
items.what: The portal processes a pseudonymous session cookie, a keyed hash of your network address for rate limits, the runs you start, and the request logs of the server and of Cloudflare.
items.retention: Access to a run expires after 24 hours, and its files are deleted after 7 days; a one-line index entry and a cost entry remain.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
controller.body: The data controller is Mario Gutiérrez, independent developer, who runs the portal. Contact: {contact}.

cookie.heading: Session cookie
cookie.body: The portal sets one pseudonymous session cookie so that it can show you your own runs and nobody else’s. It holds a random identifier, not your name or an account. It is marked HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict: it is sent only over HTTPS, cannot be read by page scripts, and is never sent with requests started on other sites.

rate-limits.heading: Rate limits
rate-limits.body: To enforce rate limits, the server keeps a keyed hash of your network address (for IPv6, of its /64 prefix): an HMAC with a secret the server rotates, so the address cannot be recovered from the table. The tables live in memory and are bounded. It is used for nothing else.

runs.heading: Runs and model outputs
runs.body: When you start a run, the server stores its contents: the task, the model outputs, the evidence records and proof statuses, the recommendation and any decision you record. Access to the run through your session expires after 24 hours, and the run’s files are deleted whole after 7 days.

items.runs: Run files: deleted whole 7 days after the run. Two things outlive them: a one-line entry in the run index (run id, time and final hash) and the run’s cost entry in the live-mode budget ledger. Neither holds the run’s text.
items.sessions: Session records: the SHA-256 hash of your session’s identifier, with when the session started and when it ends, kept on the server’s disk until the session ends (24 hours at most), so that a restart of the server does not end it. The identifier itself is never written to disk.
items.addresses: Keyed hashes of network addresses: in memory only, in bounded tables; they are not written to disk and go when the server restarts or the table evicts them.
items.logs: Request logs of the server, logs of the cloudflared tunnel and the host’s system logs: they follow the host’s log rotation.
items.operator: The operator’s detail log, keyed by request id, which holds the detail of failures for diagnosis: kept by the operator and not published.

meta.heading: Live calls to Meta
meta.body: Live Meta runs send to Meta’s Model API the preset task, the snapshot’s evidence records and the earlier model outputs of the run (proposals, critiques and evaluations), together with a pseudonymous safety identifier derived from your session, not your name or network address. No text you type is sent, because live mode accepts presets only. Meta Platforms, Inc. processes this data in the United States under Meta’s own terms.

cloudflare.heading: Cloudflare and Turnstile
cloudflare.body: The portal is served through Cloudflare, which processes your IP address and request data to deliver the site, block abuse and apply the territory block, and keeps traffic statistics for every site it proxies. Cloudflare may set its own cookies (such as __cf_bm and cf_clearance) for its bot protection. Cloudflare Turnstile, which checks that a visitor is not an automated bot, processes IP and device signals. Cloudflare, Inc. processes this data in the United States; see <cloudflare>Cloudflare’s privacy policy</cloudflare>.

hosting.heading: Hosting
hosting.body: The portal’s server is a Linux machine administered by the owner at the owner’s hosting provider (country: {hostingCountry}), behind Cloudflare. It stores the data described in this notice.

basis.heading: Legal basis and your rights
basis.body: For visitors in the EU, the EEA and the UK: the session cookie, the rate limits, the bot check, the territory block and the request logs rest on the owner’s legitimate interest in running a public research prototype safely; the runs you start, and the live calls to Meta they involve, are processed because you ask for them. There are no accounts. You can ask the owner, at the contact above, for access to or deletion of the data linked to your session or to a run id; run files are deleted after 7 days in any case. You can also complain to your data protection authority.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside your country
transfers.body: Live calls go to Meta Platforms, Inc. and the site is delivered through Cloudflare, Inc.; both process the data described above in the United States, under their own terms and safeguards.

browser.heading: Settings in your browser
browser.body: Theme, language, motion, explanation level and whether you closed the tour are saved in your browser’s local storage. They never leave your device, and you can remove them in <settings>Settings</settings>.

not-done.heading: What the portal does not do
not-done.body: The pages contain no analytics or tracking scripts, no advertising and no cross-site tracking, and no data is sold or shared for marketing. Cloudflare’s traffic statistics, described above, are the only statistics kept.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Questions and requests about this notice go to the data controller, Mario Gutiérrez: {contact}.

limitations.lead: What the results of Hyphae Consensus can and cannot tell you.

integrity.heading: Integrity is not truth
integrity.body: A valid proof shows that the Hyphae recall it seals reproduces against its pinned anchor. It does not yet show that the record text you see is the text the proof sealed (audit finding HY-1), and it never shows that the record is correct, relevant or complete, or that a model actually used it.

policy.heading: The policy is fixed; its main input is not
policy.body: The recommendation comes from a deterministic runtime policy, not from a model. But the policy’s main input is the Evidence Evaluator’s judgment of each claim, and that judgment is a model output. So “models never decide” holds in form, not in substance.

outcomes.heading: Contested and abstained are normal outcomes
outcomes.body: A run that ends contested or abstained is the system reporting open objections, contradictions or gaps honestly, instead of turning uncertainty into confidence.

liveFailures.heading: A live run can fail
liveFailures.body: A live run can fail: Meta’s service can time out or return an answer the protocol refuses. A failed run decides nothing, says where it stopped, and you can start another.

labels.heading: Simulated and recorded runs are labeled
labels.body: Guided runs use scripted roles and simulated evidence and are labeled SIMULATED; a simulated proof is never shown as a real one. Archived runs keep the labels they were recorded with: a scripted run stays SIMULATED, and a live-model run with simulated proofs says so next to META MODEL. In the showcase they are shown as RECORDED, never as LIVE.

showcase.heading: What the showcase lets you re-check
showcase.body: For each recorded run whose log carries a hash chain (schema 1.1 and later), you can download its log, recompute that chain in your browser or with the read-only command line, and compare the file’s SHA-256 with the digest the server lists from the archive’s manifest; to rely on that digest, compare it yourself with the MANIFEST.json of a tagged commit of the repository. Runs recorded before schema 1.1 carry no hash chain: their records cannot be re-hashed or linked one by one, and only the file’s SHA-256 can be compared with the digest the manifest pins (where there is one), which shows that these are the archived bytes, not that no record was changed before they were archived. A run that began before schema 1.1 is chained only from its later records; each run’s page says which case applies. The proofs in those runs were verified when the runs happened; their proof and witness files are held privately and cannot be re-verified from the portal.

chain.heading: The hash chain is unsigned
chain.body: Run events are SHA-256 hash-chained, but the chain is not signed. It is tamper-evident only against a head hash exported earlier: someone who rewrites and re-hashes the whole log can produce a new chain that checks out.

evidence.heading: Synthetic evidence
evidence.body: The evidence comes from a small set of synthetic records about a demo repository, seeded by the operator. It is not production knowledge.

prototype.heading: A prototype
prototype.body: Hyphae Consensus is a hackathon prototype. The gaps found by its multi-agent (AI) audit of 27 October 2026 are documented in its repository. Protocol 1.3 closes the two fail-open paths the audit found (MA-1, RT-1) and has not yet been re-validated live; other fixes are in progress.

About.lead: Hyphae Consensus is an independent project created for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026, Indie Developer track.

independent.heading: Independent
independent.body: Hyphae Consensus is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Meta. It uses Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 model through the Meta Model API.

hyphae.heading: Hyphae
hyphae.body: Hyphae (Hyphae Core and Hyphae Agent Memory) is the owner’s own earlier open-source project, copyright Celiums Solutions LLC, licensed under Apache-2.0 (its documentation under CC-BY-SA-4.0) and frozen at commit 418a3da before the hackathon began. Hyphae Consensus uses it only through its public interfaces and does not claim it as new work. The name “Hyphae” is a trademark of Celiums Solutions LLC, used with its permission. Hyphae’s source: github.com/Hyphae-Research-Foundation/hyphae.

license.heading: License
license.body: This repository is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, copyright 2026 Mario Gutiérrez. The license covers this repository only: Hyphae is not relicensed and keeps its own license and notices.

ai.heading: AI assistance
ai.body: Development used AI coding assistants: Meta’s Muse Code (with Muse Wonder Full) and Anthropic’s Claude. Commits where Claude contributed carry a Co-Authored-By trailer. All inference inside the product uses Meta’s Model API only (muse-wonder-1.0); the coding assistants are not part of the product and never appear in receipts. The owner reviews and authorizes every change.
